title: Weak elliptic-curve families and structural leads
definition: A record identifies a scoped mathematical family or condition. A geometric covering, a selected-subgroup reduction, a class-support witness and an arithmetic optimization carry different evidence statuses.
completeness_contract: An exhaustive statement applies only to its declared field, parameter family, input law and hypotheses. Family overlaps are retained. Unknown membership is not a negative result.

sources.title: Smart: The Discrete Logarithm Problem on Elliptic Curves of Trace One (1999)
Pohlig-Hellman: An Improved Algorithm for Computing Logarithms over GF(p) (1978)
Menezes-Okamoto-Vanstone: Reducing elliptic curve logarithms to finite-field logarithms (1991/1993)
Momose-Chao: Elliptic curves with weak coverings over cubic extensions (2009, revised 2013)
Joux-Vitse: Cover and Decomposition Index Calculus (2011, EUROCRYPT 2012)
ISO-1: exact two-branch support, independent census and construction (2026)
ISO-1: larger odd extension degrees and norm-one controls (2026)

families.name: Anomalous prime-field curves
families.domain: Nonsingular E over F_p, p prime, selected group E(F_p).
families.recognition: Exact N = p, equivalently trace t = 1. Near equality is a different condition.
properties: The selected full group has characteristic order p.
Prime-field and extension-field hypotheses are recorded separately.
families.find_members: For a fixed prime, a certified trace-one enumeration or trace-prescribed construction gives members. Exact counting certifies the predicate.
families.exhaustive_scope: All nonsingular prime-field models whose certified trace equals one; equivalent models require identity-aware deduplication.
families.subgroup_gate: Specify the characteristic-order group and the hypotheses of the cited p-adic reduction.
families.cost_gate: Retain construction/counting and reduction verification costs for an implementation.

families.name: Insufficient selected-subgroup size
families.domain: A specified cyclic subgroup with verified order r and a declared work/security target.
families.recognition: Assess generic work against r, rather than field bit length or the ambient curve order.
properties: A large field can contain a small selected group.
There is no context-free bit-length threshold in this catalogue.
families.find_members: Fix the required subgroup-size contract and enumerate/count admissible models in a bounded parameter family.
families.exhaustive_scope: Exact only for the declared subgroup-order threshold and counted family.
families.subgroup_gate: Order and subgroup definition or generator must be known.
families.cost_gate: Use the same-target generic reference and resource envelope when measuring a comparison.

families.name: Smooth or highly factored selected group order
families.domain: A cyclic selected group with certified factorization r = product of prime powers.
families.recognition: The relevant factorization is that of the selected group order. A small ambient cofactor does not establish this condition.
properties: Prime-power component structure controls the known decomposition of the group problem.
Unfactored orders remain unknown.
families.find_members: Use order-prescribed bounded families and retain a certified order factorization.
families.exhaustive_scope: All selected orders satisfying the stated smoothness bound within the counted family.
families.subgroup_gate: Factorization of r and the chosen cyclic group are required.
families.cost_gate: Charge order factoring and component costs; a factorization alone is not a measured runtime.

families.name: Low embedding-degree pairing reductions
families.domain: E over F_Q, prime r distinct from the characteristic, with a nondegenerate suitable pairing and embedding degree k.
families.recognition: Compute k = ord_r(Q) and verify the transfer hypotheses for the selected r-subgroup.
properties: MOV and related Tate-pairing reductions lead to finite-field groups.
Small k is a structural fact; comparative weakness depends on the target field Q^k and group r.
families.find_members: Enumerate trace/order or pairing-family parameters in a declared finite domain; certify r and k.
families.exhaustive_scope: Relative to the fixed family, subgroup and embedding-degree bound.
families.subgroup_gate: Nondegeneracy and preservation of the selected r-subgroup must be established.
families.cost_gate: Include transfer and the destination field model/cost, compared on the same target contract.

families.name: Supersingular elliptic curves
families.domain: E over F_(p^m), with prime r different from p and the small exceptional subgroup cases handled explicitly.
families.recognition: Supersingularity is exact from the characteristic/trace criterion or a certified endomorphism computation.
properties: Supersingular elliptic curves have bounded pairing embedding degree for the relevant prime-to-characteristic subgroups.
The ordinary quadratic-order volcano model does not apply.
families.find_members: Use published supersingular parameter families or a complete bounded trace/model enumeration.
families.exhaustive_scope: For a fixed finite field, complete supersingular enumeration has an explicit finite domain.
families.subgroup_gate: Record r and the actual embedding field; supersingularity alone is not the selected-subgroup cost comparison.
families.cost_gate: Pairing transfer and destination field cost remain separate.

families.name: Genus-3 cubic norm-one branch
families.domain: K = F_(p^6), q = p^2, p > 3; nonsingular y^2 = x(x-alpha)(x-alpha^q), alpha outside F_q, with allowed twists.
families.recognition: Model: norm-one Legendre parameter. Class: the exact cubic torus/CM intersection for ordinary t = 2 modulo 4 and D_K < -4; the complete finite oracle handles exceptional units.
properties: Full rational 2-torsion.
v2(f_pi) >= 2 is necessary, with f_pi the Frobenius-order conductor.
Selected 2-quotient CM orders have c dividing f_pi/4.
families.find_members: Enumerate nonidentity parameters in the torus of order p^4+p^2+1. Hilbert 90 supplies alpha; quotient by documented equivalences.
families.exhaustive_scope: Complete for the declared hyperelliptic branch. Seven complete class censuses are available through p37.
families.subgroup_gate: The covering and any source route need kernel/order compatibility for a specified subgroup.
families.cost_gate: CM support generation, parameter reconstruction, source route and destination computation have separate costs.

families.name: Genus-3 nonsplit quadratic branch
families.domain: K = F_(p^6), q = p^2, p > 3; y^2 = (x^2-d)(x-alpha)(x-alpha^q), d a base-field nonsquare, alpha outside F_q.
families.recognition: Model: the quadratic torus test on j. Class: the exact selected-floor CM intersection for ordinary t = 2 modulo 4 and D_K < -4; exceptional-unit cases use the complete finite oracle.
properties: Exactly one rational nonidentity 2-torsion point; a rational 2-quotient has full 2-torsion.
Selected CM conductors satisfy c | f_pi and v2(c) = v2(f_pi).
The invariant has exact absolute degree six.
families.find_members: Enumerate nonidentity parameters in the torus of order p^4-p^2+1 in F_(p^12), then use the proved Cayley reconstruction and allowed twists.
families.exhaustive_scope: Complete for the declared branch and its finite torus domain.
families.subgroup_gate: Specify subgroup compatibility for cover and source transport.
families.cost_gate: The degree-18 per-factor decision does not include CM support generation.

families.name: Cubic-extension (2,2) Type I coverings
families.domain: K = F_(q^3), q odd; the four roots alpha, alpha^q, beta, beta^q are distinct, with alpha,beta outside F_q and the published leading-coefficient condition.
families.recognition: Membership uses the Type I condition of Momose-Chao; their direct test is a quadratic-equation test.
properties: Full rational 2-torsion after normalization.
The resulting genus-3 covering may be hyperelliptic or non-hyperelliptic.
families.find_members: Use y^2 = (x-alpha)(x-alpha^q)(x-beta)(x-beta^q), with the recorded exclusions and model equivalences.
families.exhaustive_scope: This parameter family under the paper's isogeny condition; no complete local isogeny-class support census is yet attached.
families.subgroup_gate: Use the actual covering kernel and selected subgroup.
families.cost_gate: Cover construction and destination geometry/solver cost require their own receipts.

families.name: Cubic-extension (2,2) Type II coverings
families.domain: K = F_(q^3), L = F_(q^6), q odd; alpha in L outside F_(q^2) and K.
families.recognition: The published conjugate-root configuration and its Legendre normalization determine membership and twist conditions.
properties: Root configuration alpha, alpha^(q^3), alpha^q, alpha^(q^4).
The Legendre leading-coefficient square class depends on q modulo four.
families.find_members: Enumerate the admissible alpha domain of the published quartic; retain its field of definition and normalization.
families.exhaustive_scope: The specified Type II family under the isogeny condition; no local fast recognition or complete class oracle is claimed here.
families.subgroup_gate: Establish the covering's field and kernel on the selected subgroup.
families.cost_gate: Construction and destination computation are unmeasured locally.

families.name: Hyperelliptic locus within the (2,2) families
families.domain: An admissible Type I or Type II configuration from Momose-Chao.
families.recognition: The stated PGL2(F_q) transformation represented by a trace-zero invertible matrix relating the two root parameters is the hyperellipticity condition.
properties: This is a geometric subcase of the Type I/II families, rather than a disjoint count.
Different coverings of an elliptic model can coexist.
families.find_members: Apply the paper's involution condition to the admissible root parameters, retaining its hypotheses.
families.exhaustive_scope: The conditional locus within the published (2,2) configurations.
families.subgroup_gate: Use the chosen covering and subgroup, rather than inferring transfer from a family name.
families.cost_gate: A geometric test has a different cost from complete source construction and solving.

families.name: Characteristic-two GHS descent families
families.domain: Ordinary binary curves over a chosen extension K/F_q satisfying the published descent hypotheses.
families.recognition: Compute the Frobenius span of the coefficients, then verify the descended cover genus and geometry.
properties: The coefficient span and extension structure govern the cover.
An extension degree alone is not a weakness certificate.
families.find_members: Choose bounded coefficient/Frobenius-span families, construct the published cover, and verify its map.
families.exhaustive_scope: Only the declared descent construction and bounded coefficient space.
families.subgroup_gate: The induced transfer must preserve the selected subgroup and avoid its kernel.
families.cost_gate: Include cover construction, field conversion and the destination solver; genus alone is insufficient.

families.name: Generalized Weil-descent cover families
families.domain: A specified extension field, descent construction and covering hypothesis.
families.recognition: A verified covering and its induced group map establish geometry; the resulting genus may exceed the original GHS case.
properties: Generalizations enlarge the parameter family.
They can change hyperellipticity and destination arithmetic.
families.find_members: Enumerate the prescribed coefficient space for a chosen published construction, with maps and genus retained.
families.exhaustive_scope: Construction-specific, rather than all extension-field curves.
families.subgroup_gate: Selected subgroup preservation is required.
families.cost_gate: Measure the resulting destination problem and all construction phases.

families.name: Larger odd-degree cubic norm-one models
families.domain: K = F_(q^n), q = p^2, n odd, n >= 3; alpha outside F_q and lambda of relative norm one.
families.recognition: The norm-one model condition and rational 2-quotient torsion controls are proved in the larger-degree evidence.
properties: The cubic 2-depth restriction extends to the recorded odd-degree domain.
The degree-six CM class theorem is not silently promoted to every n.
families.find_members: Use nonidentity relative norm-one parameters and constructive Hilbert 90.
families.exhaustive_scope: The explicit functional model family; efficient large-field class-support discovery remains unresolved.
families.subgroup_gate: Record the actual cover and selected subgroup for the extension degree.
families.cost_gate: Larger-degree arithmetic controls do not supply a destination-solver comparison.

families.name: Larger odd-degree quadratic Cayley models
families.domain: K = F_(q^n), L = F_(q^(2n)), q odd and n >= 3 odd; nonidentity lambda in the torus of order (q^n+1)/(q+1).
families.recognition: Constructive quadratic-base Hilbert 90 and a base norm equation recover alpha even when the inverse exponent does not exist.
properties: Sixteen degree-10/14 controls pass; eight have noncoprime section gcd five.
For prime relative n, the specified compositum cover has genus 1+2^(n-2)(n-2), giving 25 and 161 at n=5,7.
families.find_members: Enumerate torus parameters in a finite chosen field, then apply the proved reconstruction.
families.exhaustive_scope: The functional family and specified cover; no minimum-genus or universal class-support statement is added.
families.subgroup_gate: A specified subgroup and induced covering map remain separate requirements.
families.cost_gate: Controls establish reconstruction and geometry; source discovery and destination solving retain separate costs.

families.name: Selected points contained in a proper subfield group
families.domain: E and the selected group/points are actually defined over a proper subfield.
families.recognition: Verify Frobenius-fixed coefficients and points, and the selected subgroup's membership in the smaller group.
properties: Ambient field bit length can overstate the selected problem's field.
Coefficients in a subfield alone do not establish point or subgroup containment.
families.find_members: Construct over a chosen subfield and explicitly specify the subgroup retained on extension.
families.exhaustive_scope: Relative to the chosen subfield and point/group condition.
families.subgroup_gate: Actual selected points and group must be contained in the subfield model.
families.cost_gate: Compare the smaller-field problem and any coordinate conversion.

families.name: Isogeny classes containing a covering-family representative
families.domain: An ordinary class over a specified field, a covering family, and a source model.
families.recognition: An exact class oracle or a verified witness establishes support. A capped or restricted walk leaves the label unresolved.
properties: Model membership and class support differ.
The p7 combined oracle is exact; 512 large-field bounded searches leave class labels unresolved.
families.find_members: Use the selected-family class criterion and reconstruct a passing representative; retain a certified route from the fixed source when one is constructed.
families.exhaustive_scope: Only the class/family oracle whose completeness is proved; finite walk policies are separately bounded.
families.subgroup_gate: Every route degree and kernel must be compatible with the specified subgroup.
families.cost_gate: CM support, failed attempts, route maps, transport, reconstruction and destination solving are separate phases.

families.name: CM field, class number and conductor signals
families.domain: Ordinary curves with exact or explicitly bounded order information.
families.recognition: Separate the Frobenius conductor from the actual endomorphism-order conductor and retain uncertainty.
properties: Class number can inform enumeration and route hypotheses.
Equal class numbers can coexist with different covering-family support.
families.find_members: Organize certified discriminants/orders and investigate a declared family-specific criterion.
families.exhaustive_scope: A signal inventory; no universal weakness classification follows from this property.
families.subgroup_gate: Needed only after an actual map or solver route is proposed.
families.cost_gate: No solver or end-to-end gain is assigned from class number alone.

families.name: Efficient endomorphisms and Frobenius symmetries
families.domain: A specified curve and subgroup on which the endomorphism action is established.
families.recognition: Record the actual map, its subgroup action and orbit/decomposition properties.
properties: GLV/GLS or Frobenius structure can improve scalar arithmetic and generic constants.
A known endomorphism is not automatically a special curve-class reduction.
families.find_members: Use published endomorphism families with exact parameters and independent map checks.
families.exhaustive_scope: The named construction or symmetry family.
families.subgroup_gate: Verify preservation and the correct eigenvalue/action, rather than selecting an unverified polynomial root.
families.cost_gate: Arithmetic and generic constants need their own measured contracts.

families.name: Rational torsion and twist/order patterns
families.domain: A curve over a fixed field, with certified torsion and twist/order information.
families.recognition: Record exact rational torsion and the family it informs; retain unfactored group orders as unknown.
properties: Full 2-torsion and one rational 2-point distinguish the two ISO-1 model branches.
A small torsion factor alone does not determine selected-subgroup weakness.
families.find_members: Use torsion-prescribed models and certify their group conditions.
families.exhaustive_scope: The torsion property or a declared torsion-prescribed family.
families.subgroup_gate: Specify the chosen group and treatment of the cofactor.
families.cost_gate: A structural filter is not a completed source-to-destination cost.

families.name: Twist and subgroup validation conditions
families.domain: A specified point-input and validation contract, together with curve/twist subgroup data.
families.recognition: Assess permitted point domains and subgroup checks under the actual contract.
properties: Twist order is relevant to some input contracts.
This is an implementation condition, not a universal curve hardness label.
families.find_members: Maintain defensive validation fixtures for the explicitly supported curve and twist domains.
families.exhaustive_scope: The declared validation contract and allowed point domains.
families.subgroup_gate: The protocol's subgroup/cofactor policy is part of the record.
families.cost_gate: No curve-level comparative solver cost is inferred.

families.name: Singular cubic input domain
families.domain: A purported elliptic model whose discriminant vanishes.
families.recognition: Certify nonsingularity before admitting an elliptic-curve record.
properties: A singular cubic has different geometry and group structure.
It is kept outside the nonsingular elliptic-family inventory.
families.find_members: Retain boundary fixtures for the model-validity check; catalogue them as rejected elliptic inputs.
families.exhaustive_scope: The exact model-validity predicate.
families.subgroup_gate: Nonsingular group definitions are required for elliptic entries.
families.cost_gate: No elliptic solver benchmark is attached to a rejected model.

relations.condition: Relevant prime-to-characteristic subgroup and verified pairing hypotheses; actual target field and cost are still required.
Full rational 2-torsion and the branch-scoped Frobenius 2-depth restriction.
One rational nonidentity 2-point, with a full-2 rational quotient.
Apply the published Type I configuration and involution hypotheses.
Apply the published Type II configuration and involution hypotheses.
The model is a direct representative; construction from another source remains a separate route question.
The model is a direct representative, in its exact field and twist.
Relative degree n = 3 and the prime-field-square hypotheses of the exact class theorem.
Relative degree n = 3 and q = p^2, p > 3.
A family-specific exact intersection or constructed representative is required.

growth_requirements: Add independently validated Type I and Type II recognition before assigning those model labels.
Add source-linked anomalous, embedding-degree and binary-descent fixtures with specified subgroups.
Obtain on-demand CM support or an equivalent complete oracle for independently sampled large classes.
Retain representative construction, subgroup transfer and destination solver costs as separate obligations.
Expand finite parameter domains with immutable protocols, exact model IDs and retained unsuccessful rows.
